definition.def: If you carry out a survey, you try to find out detailed information about a lot of different people or things, usually by asking people a series of questions.
examples: The council conducted a survey of the uses to which farm buildings are put.
According to the survey, overall world trade has also slackened.

definition.def: If you survey a number of people, companies, or organizations, you try to find out information about their opinions or behaviour, usually by asking them a series of questions.
examples: Business Development Advisers surveyed 211 companies for the report. [VERB noun]
Only 18 percent of those surveyed opposed the idea. [VERB-ed]

definition.def: If you survey something, you look at or consider the whole of it carefully.
examples: He pushed himself to his feet and surveyed the room. [VERB noun]
He surveys American politics with a conservative world view. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you give something a brief survey or a quick survey, you look at or consider all of it quickly, but not in detail.
examples: ...a brief survey of some important books on astrology.
He sniffed the perfume she wore, then gave her a quick survey.

definition.def: If someone carries out a survey of an area of land, they examine it and measure it, usually in order to make a map of it.
examples: ...the organizer of the geological survey of India.
The scientists conducted two aerial surveys followed by two ground surveys.

definition.def: If someone surveys an area of land, they examine it and measure it, usually in order to make a map of it.
examples: The council commissioned geological experts to survey the cliffs. [VERB noun]

definition.def: A survey is a careful examination of the condition and structure of a house, usually carried out in order to give information to a person who wants to buy it. [mainly British]
examples: ...a structural survey undertaken by a qualified surveyor.

definition.def: If someone surveys a house, they examine it carefully and report on its structure, usually in order to give advice to a person who is thinking of buying it. [mainly British]
examples: ...the people who surveyed the house for the mortgage. [VERB noun]
